The IEJoin rewrite for a left join with a cross-and-filter predicate gets reached through process_join and try_rewrite_join_type, and since maintain_order defaults to None the join type stays Left. Coalesce is already set to KeepColumns from resolve_join_where, so I'm now checking how projection pushdown treats the Join arm when the left and right keys are plain columns.

I'm tracing why projection pushdown marks the coalesce as CoalesceColumns for this IEJoin: `y` isn't in the left schema or the projected output, and the predicate names are empty, so the condition passes. That looks wrong, since the coalescing assumes equi-join keys with equal values, which doesn't hold for IEJoin. I'm now working through how det_join_schema then drops the right key `y` and which columns end up on each side.

I'm working through the projected names for the right side, where the output ends up as `[k, y]`. With the coalesce in place, `y` gets dropped from the output and `k` keeps its plain name, so the final projection just renames `k` back to `k_right`. That looks fine on paper, but the IEJoin executor ignores `should_coalesce` and still returns all of the right columns, `[k, y]`.

I'm questioning whether the physical IEJoin output really matches the planner's schema, since the executor ignores the coalesce flag and may still return the right columns in their original order. If the right input is ordered as [y, k], the post-projection `k_right` lookup would pick up `y`'s values, which would explain the zero results the team is seeing. I'm now checking whether the `select("x")` case behaves differently.

I'm checking the `select("k", "k_right")` case next: the left side keeps `k` and `x`, the right side keeps `k` and `y`, and with the coalesce `y` gets dropped while `k` picks up the `k_right` name. The projected names already line up with the output schema, so no extra post-projection should be attached, and I need to see whether the physical join output actually matches that.

I'm checking whether the physical output order matches the planner's schema, since a positional lookup would explain the wrong values. The `select("k", "k_right")` case seems to resolve correctly on paper, so I'm trying to find where the ordering actually diverges.

Now I'm checking whether the `k_right` lookup holds up once the columns are read by position, since the in-memory projection could reorder `k` and `x` relative to the planner's schema. The IEJoin key ordering looks right on paper, so I'm also looking at whether the executor's rename of clashing right-side columns to `k_right` could be shifting which physical column ends up where.

Now I'm checking how the right-side columns are ordered in the join input, since a positional lookup for `k_right` would pick up `y` if `y` comes first.

I'm checking whether streaming changes the picture here: the IEJoin lowering falls back to an in-memory join, which rebuilds the join node with its own input schemas, so the column order could differ from what the planner assumed.

I'm checking whether the streaming lowering of the post-join Select changes the column order, since it resolves names against the planner's output schema. I'm also looking at whether the right input could arrive as [y, k] and make a positional lookup pick up `y`.

I'm checking whether the streaming engine's in-memory join fallback rebuilds its input schemas, which could reorder the right-side columns so that a positional lookup for `k_right` picks up `y` instead.

I'm checking whether the streaming engine's lowering of the post-join select could resolve `k` against a different column order than the physical join emits, since a positional lookup would explain the wrong values.

I'm checking whether the right-side input could come in as [y, k], since DataFrameScan projection pushdown might keep the names in projected order rather than the original schema order. With both columns projected the subset shortcut doesn't apply, so the simple-projection branch is what decides the final order.

I'm checking whether the right-side input could be ordered [y, k] and whether a simple projection node would reorder it, since a positional lookup for `k_right` would then pick up `y`.

I'm now reasoning that the streaming post-projection resolves `k_right` by position, and the observed output (columns named `k` and `y`) would fit a physical right-side order of [y, k].

I'm checking whether the streaming right-side input could be ordered [y, k], since a positional lookup for `k_right` would then pick up `y`. That would also explain why `select("x")` returns the right values while `select("k", "k_right")` shows columns named `k` and `y`.

I'm checking whether the streaming engine's SimpleProjection after the join might attach to the right side and reorder the columns to [k, y], which would rule out the positional mismatch I was chasing.

I'm noticing that the right side has only two columns, so the projection of `{k, y}` matches its full width and no pruning gets pushed into that input. That would leave the right side in its original `[y, k]` order, which fits the streaming `k_right` lookup picking up `y`.

I'm working out the output schema for `select("k", "k_right")`: the left side keeps `[x, k]` and the right side stays `[y, k]`, so after coalescing and renaming, the projected columns come out as `[k, k_right]`.

I'm checking the streaming case for the `select("k", "k_right")` projection: the physical output is [x, k, y, k_right], so a positional lookup for `k_right` lands on `y`, which explains the mismatched column names. The in-memory engine selects by name, so it returns the right columns. The other variants look fine because the coalesce only drops `y` when it isn't projected.

I'm checking whether the inner-join path rewrites to IEJoin, since the coalesce rule only matches Inner or Left and would skip that type. With no optimizer flags, predicate pushdown doesn't run, so the cross-and-filter form would stay, but projection pushdown wouldn't run either, so that case doesn't matter here.

I'm pinning down the root cause: the projection-pushdown coalesce rule assumes an equi-join, but IEJoin keys are inequalities, so dropping the right key is wrong. The streaming SimpleProjection then reads the wrong column by position. The fix is to require a pure equi-join before coalescing.

I'm settling on the fix: the coalesce should only apply to a pure equi-join, so I'd check for the `Equi` options variant before dropping the right key. The `Equi` check is conservative, but it keeps IEJoin from having its right key dropped, which is what leaves the schema out of step with the physical columns.

I'm going to check whether an inner join also gets rewritten into IEJoin, by looking at how the inner-join path sets the join type.
